name: Arc
description: Design-led browser with a sidebar, Spaces and Boosts. The Browser Company sunsets it on Dec 22, 2026 in favour of Dia.

name: Brave
description: Privacy-focused Chromium browser with built-in ad blocking, Shields and optional BAT crypto rewards.

name: BrowserOS
description: Open-source Chromium fork with built-in AI agents that run locally and keep data private.

name: Browsh
description: Modern text-based browser that renders pages through headless Firefox into the terminal, with graphics and video.

name: Carbonyl
description: Chromium running inside a terminal, rendering pages with Unicode blocks. No commits since early 2023.

name: ChatGPT Atlas
description: OpenAI's Chromium-based AI browser for macOS. Launched Oct 2025, shut down Aug 9, 2026.

name: Chromium
description: Open-source project from Google that provides the code base for Chrome and most Blink-based browsers.

name: Cốc Cốc
description: Vietnamese Chromium browser with Vietnamese-optimized search and media downloading.

name: Comet
description: Perplexity's AI browser with a built-in assistant that researches and acts across tabs.

name: Cromite
description: Privacy-and-ad-blocking Chromium fork continuing Bromite; desktop builds available for Windows.

name: Dia
description: AI-first browser from The Browser Company (Atlassian) with a built-in chat assistant on every tab.

name: Dillo
description: Extremely lightweight graphical browser in FLTK with no JavaScript, focused on speed and tiny footprint.

name: Disco
description: Google Labs experimental Chromium browser for macOS that turns open tabs into Gemini-generated GenTabs apps.

name: ELinks
description: Feature-rich text-mode browser with tabs, colours and scripting; maintained as the rkd77 fork.

name: Falkon
description: Lightweight KDE Qt browser using QtWebEngine.

name: Fellou
description: Agentic AI browser that automates multi-step web workflows and research.

name: FireDragon
description: LibreWolf-based Firefox fork from the Garuda Linux project with extra privacy, performance and theming tweaks.

name: Firefox
description: Mozilla's flagship open-source browser built on the Gecko engine, with a large add-on ecosystem.

name: Firefox Developer Edition
description: Firefox channel aimed at web developers, with early features and extra developer tooling enabled.

name: Firefox ESR
description: Extended Support Release of Firefox with long-lived major versions for organisations and slow-moving deployments.

name: Firefox Nightly
description: Daily pre-release build of Firefox for testing the newest, unfinished features.

name: Floorp
description: Japanese Firefox-based browser with a highly customizable UI, vertical tabs and workspaces.

name: Flow Browser
description: Open-source Electron browser with spaces, sidebar and a modern UI.

name: Glide
description: Extensible, keyboard-focused Firefox fork configurable with TypeScript, inspired by Vim-style workflows.

name: GNOME Web (Epiphany)
description: The GNOME desktop's default browser, using WebKitGTK with a minimal interface and built-in tracker blocking.

name: Google Chrome
description: The most widely used web browser, built by Google on Chromium with Google sync and services.

name: Helium
description: Minimal privacy-first browser based on ungoogled-chromium with uBlock Origin built in.

name: Internet Explorer
description: Microsoft's Trident-based browser bundled with Windows from 1995; support ended June 2022.

name: Island Enterprise Browser
description: Enterprise-focused Chromium browser with built-in policy controls and data protections.

name: Konqueror
description: KDE's long-running file manager and web browser in one, now rendering with QtWebEngine.

name: Ladybird
description: Truly independent browser with its own engine (LibWeb), not based on Chromium, Gecko or WebKit. Pre-alpha; first alpha due late 2026.

name: LibreWolf
description: Privacy- and security-hardened Firefox fork with telemetry removed and uBlock Origin preinstalled.

name: Links
description: Text and graphics-mode browser (Links2) with tables, frames and menu-driven interface.

name: Luakit
description: Fast, extensible, micro-framework browser using WebKit2GTK and configurable with Lua.

name: Lynx
description: One of the oldest web browsers still maintained (1992), a fully text-based browser for terminals.

name: Mercury
description: Firefox fork with compiler optimizations and patches from LibreWolf, Waterfox and GNU IceCat.

name: Microsoft Edge
description: Microsoft's Chromium-based default Windows browser with vertical tabs, Copilot and enterprise features.

name: Microsoft Edge Legacy
description: Original EdgeHTML-based Edge shipped with Windows 10 (2015–2021), replaced by Chromium Edge.

name: Min
description: Minimal Electron-based browser with fast search, built-in ad blocking and tasks.

name: Mullvad Browser
description: Privacy browser by Mullvad and the Tor Project that uses Tor Browser's anti-fingerprinting without the Tor network.

name: Naver Whale
description: South Korean Chromium browser by Naver with sidebar, split view and Naver AI.

name: Netscape Navigator
description: Dominant 1990s browser by Netscape that introduced JavaScript and SSL; classic versions ended in 2008.

name: NetSurf
description: Small, fast, lightweight browser with its own engine (Hubbub, LibCSS, Duktape) running on many platforms including RISC OS.

name: Nook
description: Open-source, sidebar-first minimal macOS browser with Rooms for grouping tasks; positioned as an Arc-style alternative.

name: Norton Neo
description: Free AI-native browser from Gen Digital (Norton) with built-in VPN, phishing protection and a proactive AI assistant.

name: Nyxt
description: Keyboard-driven, programmable 'hacker's browser' written in Common Lisp using WebKitGTK; Emacs-like extensibility.

name: Opera
description: Norwegian Chromium browser with built-in free VPN, ad blocker, sidebar messengers and Workspaces.

name: Opera 12 (Presto)
description: Last Presto-engine release of Opera (2012), known for speed, mouse gestures and built-in tools.

name: Opera Air
description: Opera edition focused on mindfulness, with breathing exercises, guided meditations and focus music.

name: Opera GX
description: Gaming-oriented Opera edition with CPU/RAM/network limiters, Twitch integration and themed UI.

name: Opera Neon
description: Opera's agentic AI browser that can perform tasks on the web for the user.

name: Orion
description: Kagi's privacy-focused WebKit browser for macOS that supports both Chrome and Firefox extensions; Linux version in beta.

name: Otter Browser
description: Qt browser aiming to recreate the classic Opera 12 UI.

name: Pale Moon
description: Independent, highly customizable browser on the Goanna engine and UXP platform, forked from pre-Australis Firefox.

name: Pissandshittium
description: Joke Chromium fork with funny UI strings and colours like 'Literal Shit'. Its own FAQ begs you not to daily-drive it.

name: Polypane
description: Browser for web developers that shows many synced viewports side by side.

name: qutebrowser
description: Keyboard-driven, vim-like browser built with Python and Qt WebEngine.

name: Responsively App
description: Open-source developer browser with multi-device previews that mirror interactions.

name: Safari
description: Apple's default browser for macOS, built on WebKit with tight system integration and strong power efficiency.

name: Safari Technology Preview
description: Apple's experimental Safari channel that previews upcoming WebKit and Safari features for developers.

name: Servo
description: Parallel browser engine written in Rust, now hosted by Linux Foundation Europe, with a servoshell demo browser.

name: SigmaOS
description: WebKit-based macOS browser with vertical tabs and workspaces aimed at productivity; development has slowed.

name: Supermium
description: Chromium fork keeping modern Chrome features running on Windows 7/8/Vista and XP.

name: surf
description: Simple suckless WebKit2GTK browser with no UI chrome, controlled by keybindings and configured at compile time.

name: Thorium
description: Performance-optimized Chromium fork with compiler optimizations, extra codecs and patches.

name: Tor Browser
description: Firefox ESR-based browser that routes traffic through the Tor network for anonymity and anti-fingerprinting.

name: Ulaa
description: Privacy-focused Chromium browser by Zoho with ad blocking and work/personal modes.

name: Ungoogled Chromium
description: Chromium with Google integration and web services removed or disabled for privacy.

name: Vieb
description: Vim-inspired Electron browser for keyboard-only navigation.

name: Vimb
description: Vim-like WebKit2GTK browser with modal interface that stays out of the way.

name: Vivaldi
description: Highly customizable Chromium browser with tab stacks, tiling, built-in mail, notes and a power-user UI.

name: w3m
description: Text-based terminal browser and pager with table and frame rendering and inline image display support.

name: Waterfox
description: Privacy-focused Firefox fork that keeps full add-on support and avoids Mozilla telemetry and sponsored content.

name: Wavebox
description: Productivity browser that groups web apps and accounts into workspaces.

name: Yandex Browser
description: Russian Chromium browser by Yandex with Alice assistant, Protect security and translation.

name: Zen Browser
description: Firefox-based browser focused on a calm, minimal design with vertical tabs, workspaces and split view.
